newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close up in high volume.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close up in high volume.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks continued to climb on local buying on Thursday and turnover exceeded 100 million rupees for the first time this year, brokers said.

The all share index closed 3.49 points up at 625.89. Price gains outnumbered declines by 42 to 11. National Development Bank rose 1.75 rupees to 192 rupees, and Sampath rose one rupee to 51.25 rupees.
Turnover broke the 100 million mark for the first time in 1997, reaching 101.6 million rupees. It last breached that level on December 11, 1996, when it hit 149.4 million rupees.
"Colombo, usually foreign led, is changing. Locals are not waiting to be led by overseas buyers," said Subram Ramaswamy, deputy general manager of Bartleet Mallory Stock Brokers.

Foreign buying amounted to 22 million rupees, and foreign sales were 76 million rupees, brokers said. "Foreign buyers are still cautious," said Dihan Dedigama, a trader at brokerage John Keells. "There are many enquiries, but few orders."

The market's uptrend, which has been triggered by expectations of good corporate growth in late 1996 and in 1997, should take the index closer to 635 points, before profit-taking sets in, Ramaswamy said. --Prithi Kodagoda (941) 434319
